analysis.slower_reason: First-pass copy overhead not amortized for short prompts (3 tokens + 2 decode). The cache reads all 197 tensors via shard path AND copies them to resident storage on first access, adding overhead that isn't recovered in only 2 decode passes.
analysis.longer_generation_projection: For longer generation (100+ tokens), the cache would amortize the first-pass copy cost and provide net speedup. The break-even point is approximately 10-15 decode passes.

conclusion: B011 — WEIGHT RESIDENCY FUNCTIONALLY CERTIFIED / I/O REDUCTION PROVEN / PERFORMANCE BENEFIT NOT YET DEMONSTRATED. The cache works correctly (80% hit rate, 77.6% bytes reduction, 99.7% maps reduction, numerical equivalence maintained). The wall-time regression for short prompts (+25.2% prefill) is observed but not yet explained by measured amortization. The hypothesis that the cache becomes faster for 100+ tokens should be tested in B012, not assumed in B011's conclusion.
next_step: B012: Amortization experiment — run increasing decode lengths (1,2,8,16,32,64,128,256 tokens) comparing B010 vs B011 to find the crossover point where residency becomes faster than repeated acquisition.
